newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana's Rawlings pledges further inflation cut.
newsitem.headline: Ghana's Rawlings pledges further inflation cut.

text.p: Ghana's President Jerry Rawlings said on Tuesday that his government would continue to crack down on inflation but warned that tough measures would have to be taken because of falling gold prices and rising oil prices.
Rawlings, re-elected to a final term in December, told the opening of parliament his aim was to cut inflation, now around 35 percent year-on-year, to single digit within 18 months.
Rawlings also promised continued efforts to boost production of cocoa -- Ghana's second money earner after gold.

"While gold prices are dropping, the price of oil has in the last six months consistently reached the highest level since the Gulf War," he said. "Very tough choices will have to be made as a result of these adverse international economic factors."
He did not go into detail but fuel prices, heavily subsidised at present, are a likely target.
In 1995, Ghana exported over 1.6 million ounces of gold, earning $647.3 million. It spent $191 million on oil imports.
Rawlings pledged more help for cocoa. "Government continues its commitment to growth of cocoa production and increase of the share of world market prices paid to farmers," he said.
In 1995, Ghana imported goods worth $1.69 billion and exported goods worth $1.43 billion. "We have to progress from a nation of importers to a nation of exporters," he said.
The president said 50 companies would be approached this year about investing in Ghana's new tax-free manufacturing zones. Twelve companies have been admitted so far.
Rawlings also promised a new land law. Officials say land disputes hinder farm development and often lead to bloodshed.
